conditions.redistribute3: Three consumers; target four hot and sixteen cold partitions each
conditions.scale_redistribute6: Scale to six; target two hot and eight cold partitions each
conditions.kafka_scale6: Scale to six with classic cooperative-sticky Kafka assignment and stable per-pod group.instance.id; no targeted hot-partition map

starting_conditions: Capture the native three-consumer empty-topic map. Select the twelve lowest-numbered partitions owned by Consumer 2 before any performance outcome is observed. Freeze this hot set and initial ownership for every condition, and verify original pod UIDs, nodes, and resource declarations before traffic.
interpretation: Native scaling uses consumer-group assignment; the other conditions use explicit exclusive ownership. Differences include the coordination mechanism as well as resulting assignments. Targets are scheduled, not chosen by an adaptive controller.
technical_checks: Previously passed nonempty redistribution monitoring gate
Empty-topic native assignment capture and matching restart
Low-load native 3-to-6 technical trial: 300 aggregate msg/s, 20 warm-up + 100 evaluation + 60 drain; all acknowledgments completed; valid offsets and six active partition owners
processing_interruption: For explicit actions, retain the verified global last-completion to first-post-resume-processing gap and per-process released-to-resumed intervals. For native scaling, record each moved partition's last old-owner completion to first new-owner processing start, and owner callbacks; a group need not have a global processing pause. Record any observed global no-processing interval separately without treating unaffected consumers as paused.
transition_and_accumulation: Explicit release_requested to active_verified; also retain scheduled and actual decision times. Native: actual scale decision to first complete fresh six-owner snapshot followed by 10 seconds of valid unchanged ownership. Count distinct acknowledged-but-unfinished records at each endpoint (including warm-up), and report the net change. This is observed accumulation, not causal excess over a no-action counterfactual or exact Kafka offset lag.

recovery.rule: Consecutive valid samples with unchanged owners and nondecreasing offsets. If not observed under continued input, report unconfirmed; drain completion is a separate outcome.

outcomes: Completed evaluation-cohort mean and nearest-rank p99 latency before commit acknowledgment
Distinct successful completion throughput and 10-second bins
Total/per-partition lag and processing backlog, 30-second growth, skew and persistence
Requested consumer CPU/memory integrated over evaluation plus drain
Ownership, offset continuity, unique message identities and monitoring validity
failure_rule: No performance trial until the monitoring correction is verified. Up to three attempts only for pre-traffic ownership mismatches, preserving rejected preparations. Stop on runtime/identity/offset failure. Retain valid unfavorable outcomes. Restore original shared configuration and three stopped consumer applications.
